<!-- pr-reviewer: 17f6ce333bf48a778cfcf4105f3b4b6e2f589aee -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** There is one blocker: on a mill-turn (and on a lathe until #1265 lands), a turning section still posts through an undeclared script. If the script is a user's own milling post, that section comes out as milling.

Reviewed head `17f6ce33`, trial-merged with current `origin/main` `0757563d`. The merge was clean.

### What looks good
- **One reader of the dialect.** `at_post` matches on main's `post::dialect::work_voice` (`crates/app/src/lathe_voice.rs:167-183`). The earlier `declared_turning` is gone. After the merge, `dialect.rs` is byte-identical to main, and `speaks_turning` still delegates to `work_voice`, so there is no second parse of `capabilities`.
- **Main's rules survived the merge.** `setup_workholding::work_speed` is untouched, and so are the #1174 `verification_report_by(... work_voice)` calls in `posting.rs` / `posting_mounts.rs` / `posting_per_op.rs`.
- **Every post path reaches the door.** It is called from three places, and every entry point goes through them:
  - `posting.rs:457`: single file, the document's post, and `post_setup`.
  - `posting_mounts.rs:210`: per mount, including a setup's own post and one explicit script for all mounts.
  - `posting_per_op.rs:124`: per op.
  - MCP `post` and the `cam.post` script verb both go through `v_post`, then `post_mounts` / `post_mounts_script`.
- **The milling-section hazard from #1199 is closed on lathe and mill-turn.** Probed through the real `post_script`: a mill Face op on a mill-turn through `fanuc-lathe.cps` with its `capabilities` line removed is refused by name. The refusal names the missing manifest line, the machine and the exact line to add.
- **No legal mill program is refused.** An undeclared user mill script (`fanuc.cps` without its line) still posts a mill op on a mill and with no machine (probed).
- **Housekeeping is clean.**
  - No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests.
  - `lathe_voice.rs` is 209 lines and `lathe_voice_tests.rs` 330.
  - No goldens, recorded streams, shipped posts or snapshot PNGs are touched. The other inline test scripts are unaffected.
  - The decision file is present.
  - The body has a `Changelog:` line and closes only #1199.
  - Commit subjects are conventional.

### Local results (merged with main, Windows, debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --no-run` | built |
| camcraft-app lib (includes `lathe_voice::tests`, 4 tests) | 147 passed |
| camcraft-post lib (includes `post::dialect`, 3 tests) | 38 passed |
| lathe_workholding_mill_post | 3 passed |
| lathe_work_spindle | 5 passed |
| lathe_workholding_kinds | 10 passed, 1 ignored |
| lathe_workholding_live | 3 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| lathe_post_refusals | 11 passed |
| lathe_post | 7 passed |
| per_op_files | 9 passed |
| setup_mounts_post | 6 passed |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The quick-gate plan for this diff (app lib, lathe_work_spindle, lathe_workholding_kinds, lathe_workholding_mill_post) is a subset of the runs above.

### Undeclared script: what main + this PR does, cell by cell
Probe setup: a throwaway local test (not pushed) using the bar fixture in `lathe_workholding_mill_post.rs`, a 2000 rpm chuck, sections at 1500 rpm, posted through `post_script`. The scripts were `fanuc.cps` and `fanuc-lathe.cps` with their `capabilities` line removed.

| Machine | Turning section / on-centre drill | Milling section | C-axis section |
|---|---|---|---|
| lathe | **posts.** The undeclared *mill* script wrote `T01 M6`, `S1500 M3` for a Facing op. #1265 as it stands refuses an undeclared script on a lathe, so this cell closes once #1265 merges. | refused by name: the lathe door here; milling kinds are also family-refused | passes the door (#1265 refuses the lathe mount) |
| mill-turn | **posts.** The undeclared mill script wrote `T01 M6`, `S1500 M3` for a Facing op. #1265 as it stands takes any script on a mill-turn, so this cell stays open. | refused by name, with the manifest fix | posts, as through a milling post today |
| mill | not creatable (family door) | posts (legal, unchanged) | posts (unchanged) |
| none (reads as mill) | not creatable | posts (legal, unchanged) | posts (unchanged) |

### Requested before merge
1. **A turning section must not post through an undeclared script on a lathe or mill-turn** (`crates/app/src/lathe_voice.rs:174-190`).
   - **What happens now.** The `Undeclared` arm holds the script "to the turning rules", so a section whose `voice_of` is `WorkSpindle` passes.
   - **Why that is wrong.** If the script is a user's own milling post without the line, a turning op (or an on-centre drill) is posted as milling: tool change, `S M3` on the tool spindle, the work standing still. The probe shows exactly that on a mill-turn and on a lathe.
   - **The maintainer's rule** (2026-11-12, recorded on #1232 and PR #1265): a section that turns the work is posted only through a turning post, on a mill-turn as on a lathe. An undeclared script is not known to be one.
   - **Who closes the cell.** #1265 as written closes the lathe cell only (`Kind::MillTurn => true` in its `posting_serves::serves`), so the mill-turn cell is left to nobody.
   - **Fix.** On a machine with a work spindle, refuse every section of an undeclared script except a C (`LiveTool`) section. Use the same wording ("no `capabilities` line ... add `capabilities = 1;` ... `capabilities = 2;`").
   - **Tests to update.**
     - Extend `an_undeclared_script_is_held_to_the_door_on_a_machine_with_a_work_spindle` so `turn` and `on-centre` are refused on both machines.
     - Set `lathe_workholding_mill_post::judged`'s `("undeclared", Section::Work)` row to the door's refusal (not judged on a chucked machine). That is stricter, not looser.
     - Update the decision file's table and its line "Reading it as turning there only ever refuses (never changes a posted line)".
   - **Cost of the stricter rule.** A genuine undeclared turning script is refused too, with the one-line fix. That matches the maintainer's rule and #1265's lathe reading.

   With this change, #1213 and #1265 agree. An undeclared script posts on a mill, or with no machine. On a lathe or mill-turn it posts only C sections and is otherwise refused by name.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **The PR body is stale.** It still describes `post::dialect::declared_turning` and pins `post::dialect::tests::an_undeclared_mask_is_none_never_a_guess`. Both were dropped when main was merged. The issue's in-review comment names that pin too. Please update both so they match the head.
- **The refusal does not name the script** (its path or registry name). It says "the post script". The op name leads to the setup, and from there to its post, so this is workable. Naming it would help on a per-mount post with several scripts. It needs the label passed into `at_post`, much as #1265's `refusal` takes one.
- **Stale comment in `crates/app/src/setup_workholding.rs`** (the `(WorkVoice::Undeclared, Some(_))` arm of `work_speed`). It still says "the lathe door does not fire for it ... Whoever settles #1199 changes this arm together with `lathe_voice::at_post`". The arm itself is still right: it is the stricter reading, and now only reachable where the door passes. The comment should say what the door now does.
- **The `("undeclared", Section::Tool) => !chucked` change in the matrix test is not a loosening.** If the door regressed, the cell would flip back to "judged" and fail. Asserting the door's text in that cell would make the pin say what it guards.
- **Residual, by design of option (b):** a doc with no machine or a mill machine, posted through an undeclared *lathe* script, still meets no door. Only the script's own meridian check stands in the way; the probe saw it refuse a Face pass with "off the spindle axis meridian". This is a mislabelled document rather than a lathe one, and #1265 does not cover it either (a mill accepts any non-turning mask). It is worth a line in the decision file.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
